subject.title: fix(agents): guard stuck-session recovery with run-handle identity

question: Should OpenClaw accept `mcp.servers.*.disabled` as a supported public configuration alias, or keep `enabled` as the sole runtime configuration contract?
rationale: The current head adds a new user-facing config spelling and runtime normalization path that conflicts with the repository’s canonical-config policy; implementation correctness cannot determine whether that permanent compatibility surface is desired.

options.title: Keep one canonical MCP flag
options.body: Recommended: remove or split the alias work, keep runtime reads on `enabled`, and restore this PR to the stated embedded-agent recovery fix.

options.title: Sponsor the alias separately
options.body: Accept `disabled` as a documented public alias only in a focused MCP PR with explicit conflict semantics, docs, migration/Doctor behavior if needed, and fresh-install plus upgrade proof.

recommendation.title: Keep one canonical MCP flag
recommendation.body: Recommended: remove or split the alias work, keep runtime reads on `enabled`, and restore this PR to the stated embedded-agent recovery fix.

likelyOwner.reason: No reliable current-main blame or ownership history could be collected in the read-only environment, so an individual owner cannot be named safely.
